pageCache.pageTitle: KES Prep Opens Its Doors to Showcase Inspirational Early Years Provision - Latest News | Community | KES Prep
pageCache.text:
KES Prep Opens Its Doors to Showcase Inspirational Early Years Provision
KES Preparatory School will welcome prospective families on Friday 13 June, from 9:30am to 11:30am, for a special Early Years Open Morning. This event offers an exciting opportunity to experience first-hand the nurturing and enriching environment that sets KES Prep apart for children aged 2 to 5.
Visitors will have the chance to explore the school’s beautiful Nursery and Reception setting, including the orchard, outdoor learning classroom, and canopy area. The morning promises to be both informative and enjoyable, with a range of family-friendly activities including a petting farm, face painting, and arts and crafts.
The Open Morning comes at an exciting time for KES Prep, as the school expands its Nursery provision and undertakes a transformative redevelopment of its Reception classrooms and outdoor Playscape. New features will include natural play elements such as sandpits, a willow tunnel, and a mud kitchen — all designed to encourage imagination, creativity, and hands-on discovery.
During the event, parents will also have the opportunity to sample the nutritious meals prepared daily for pupils by the school’s on-site catering team, reflecting the school's commitment to high-quality care and wellbeing.
Headmistress at King Edward VI Preparatory School, Mys Smith, commented: “We are proud to offer a truly inspiring start to a child’s educational journey. Our Early Years setting is carefully designed to promote confidence, curiosity, and a love of learning — all within a warm, supportive community.”
With limited places remaining for the 2025 academic year, families are encouraged to register early. Bookings can be made online via the application form or by contacting the Admissions Team directly on 01794 513231.
To find out more, visit prep.kes.school.
Headmistress Mrs Rebecca Smith

pageCache.text:
KES Prep Pupil Wins National Art Competition and Secures Front Cover Feature
KES Prep is delighted to announce that Logan, one of our talented young artists, has won a top prize in the national Perfect Pets drawing competition, organised by Young Artists. His outstanding artwork has not only impressed the judges but has also earned a place on the front cover of the published book — a remarkable achievement!
The Perfect Pets competition invited children from across the country to showcase their creativity by drawing their favourite, imaginary, or ideal pet, celebrating both their artistic talents and love for animals. Logan’s success is a testament to his exceptional imagination and artistic skill, and we are incredibly proud of his accomplishment.
Young Artists has been inspiring and supporting young creatives for over 20 years, offering them a platform to develop their talents and gain national recognition. Competitions like these provide invaluable opportunities for children to express themselves and build confidence in their creative abilities.
To learn more about the competition and Young Artists, visit: www.youngartists.co.uk/competitions
Headmistress Mrs Rebecca Smith

pageCache.pageTitle: Smoothie Bikes and Fresh Thinking: A Delicious Start to a New Catering Partnership - Latest News | Community | KES Prep
pageCache.text:
Smoothie Bikes and Fresh Thinking: A Delicious Start to a New Catering Partnership
As part of our commitment to well-being, healthy eating, and interactive learning, KES Prep is delighted to announce its new partnership with Holroyd Howe, a renowned catering company that shares our ethos of nurturing young minds through fresh, seasonal, and sustainable food.
Holroyd Howe, who cater exclusively for independent schools across the UK, bring with them not only culinary expertise but a passion for food education, creativity, and pupil engagement. Their approach is simple yet transformative: fresh and nutritious meals, sourced responsibly and served with imagination.
To mark the beginning of this exciting new relationship, Holroyd Howe introduced one of their most popular food experiences: the Smoothie Bike. This innovative, pedal-powered machine challenges pupils to hop on and generate the energy required to blend their own smoothies. As they pedalled, fresh fruits and vegetables were whirled into delicious, healthy drinks — fuelled entirely by their own efforts.
The reaction from pupils was one of absolute enchantment. Fascinated by the idea of powering their own food, they queued eagerly to have a go! The experience brought together fun, fitness, and flavour in perfect harmony, sparking conversations around healthy choices, sustainability, and the joy of fresh produce.
The Smoothie Bike was more than a novelty; it encapsulated everything Holroyd Howe stands for — an emphasis on nutritious, balanced meals made with care and purpose, and delivered in ways that delight and educate in equal measure. Their offering at KES Prep will continue to champion these values through thoughtfully prepared menus, engaging food events, and an environment where mealtimes are a highlight of the day.
We are proud to partner with a team who understand that good food is not only about nutrition — it is also about community, curiosity, and care. With initiatives like the Smoothie Bike and an unwavering focus on provenance and well-being, Holroyd Howe are helping us build a positive food culture that supports every child to flourish.
We look forward to this being the first of many exciting culinary moments at KES Prep.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Right Environment Changes Everything: Why Year 3 at KES Prep Is a Perfect Starting Point  - Latest News | Community | KES Prep
pageCache.text:
The Right Environment Changes Everything: Why Year 3 at KES Prep Is a Perfect Starting Point
At KES Prep, we believe that the right environment changes everything. From the moment children join in Year 3, they are welcomed into a nurturing community where curiosity, confidence and connection flourish side by side.
As children move into this exciting stage of their Prep journey, learning takes on new depth and purpose. Small classes, specialist teaching and strong relationships form the foundation for both academic progress and personal growth. Year 3 is where pupils begin to step up — developing independence, resilience and a love of learning that will stay with them for life.
A Foundation of Emotional Safety and Connection
Deep learning starts with emotional safety. When children feel known, supported and valued, they are free to take risks, ask questions and make mistakes — knowing that each step forward is celebrated.
At KES Prep, the relationships between teachers and pupils are central to everything we do. Our small class sizes ensure that every child receives individual attention, while our experienced teachers take time to understand how each pupil learns best. This sense of belonging gives children the confidence to explore new ideas, stretch their thinking and engage fully in every lesson.
Specialist Teaching from Year 3
From Year 3 onwards, pupils benefit from an exciting and diverse curriculum led by specialist teachers. Subjects such as Performing Arts, Languages, Art, Outdoor Education, PE and Games are taught by experts who inspire creativity and curiosity.
This specialist approach encourages children to take pride in their learning, recognise their strengths and gain a sense of independence as they move between different learning spaces and subjects.
Small Classes, Big Confidence
Our small class sizes are key to the individual attention and support that define a KES Prep education. Teachers know every child — not just their learning style, but their character, interests and potential.
In this environment, children feel both challenged and cared for. They are encouraged to ask questions, express opinions and embrace new opportunities, whether that’s in the classroom, on stage, or outdoors in our beautiful grounds.
A Seamless Pathway to Senior School
As pupils move through the Prep years, their progress is carefully monitored to ensure they are ready for the next stage of their education. Those who are thriving by Year 5 are eligible for our Head’s Recommendation — a trusted route of entry to King Edward VI Senior School that recognises consistent effort, curiosity and achievement.
This pathway means there is no need for an 11+ entrance exam, removing unnecessary pressure and allowing children to continue their learning journey with confidence and continuity.
Flourishing from Year 3 and Beyond
At KES Prep, children build the skills, relationships and confidence that prepare them not only for Senior School but for life beyond. Year 3 marks the start of this empowering journey — where pupils are encouraged to explore, create and achieve in an environment that values kindness, curiosity and joy in learning.
Because when children feel safe, inspired and understood, the right environment truly does change everything.
Come and Visit Us
We would be delighted to welcome you to KES Prep to see our school in action. Come and experience our warm, nurturing environment, meet our dedicated teachers and see for yourself how children flourish here every day.
To arrange a personal visit or attend one of our upcoming open events, please contact our Admissions Team — we look forward to meeting you soon.
Headmistress Mrs Rebecca Smith

pageCache.text:
SEND
King Edward VI Preparatory School has a dedicated Learning Support team that works with children across the school to ensure that any barriers to learning are identified and supported.
At KES Prep we have always prided ourselves on our ability to offer additional support to enable children to reach their potential, and we are broadly inclusive. Where new children join the School in the older years, our admissions process is gently selective. This ensures we can meet the needs of new starters without compromising the support in place for those already at our School.
Whilst we are not always being able to support children with a high level of need, we have a dedicated learning support team that work in all areas of the School to support teachers in providing the best possible learning outcomes for all. We are immensely proud of the progress our pupils make, and none more so than those who experience additional challenges.
We recognise that all children have different strengths, weaknesses, talents and skills; helping each and every one of our children ‘find their thing’ is a big part of what we do at KES Prep, regardless of academic ability.
If you would like to discuss our additional support in further detail please contact our Head of Learning Support through the main office.

pageCache.text:
Reception and Pre-Prep Bring the Christmas Story to Life with Magical Nativity Performances
This festive season, the youngest performers at KES Prep brought the Christmas Story to life with two heart-warming Nativity productions.
The Reception children shone in their Nativity, ‘Dance to the Manger,’ showcasing their incredible Performing Arts talent and creativity. From a disco-dancing donkey to ballet-dancing shepherds, ribbon-dancing wise men, and twirling, shining stars, the children brought joy, energy, and sparkle to their performance. Their enthusiasm and dance moves captivated everyone in the audience and filled the room with festive cheer.
Meanwhile, the Pre-Prep children in Years 1 and 2 performed ‘Prickly Hay!’ — a heart-warming Nativity set in the stable, told from the perspective of the stable girls and the animals. Performing in front of family and friends, these young stars displayed confidence, joy, and excitement as they brought the story to life with creativity and spirit.
A huge thank you was extended to all the families who joined KES Prep to celebrate these special festive moments. Their support truly made the performances even more magical.
At KES Prep, Performing Arts is at the heart of the curriculum, with a strong emphasis on fostering creativity, confidence, and collaboration. The school provides a dynamic and engaging learning environment where children are inspired to explore their talents, build confidence, and grow as individuals through exciting opportunities.
Experience KES Prep in Action
Discover how KES Prep nurtures creativity, confidence, and excellence through its Performing Arts programme and broad curriculum. The next School in Action Open Morning is on Friday 7 February. To book your place, or learn more about life at KES Prep, contact the school today.

pageCache.pageTitle: KES Prep: A Nurturing and Inspiring Learning Environment for Every Child - Latest News | Community | KES Prep
pageCache.text:
KES Prep: A Nurturing and Inspiring Learning Environment for Every Child
King Edward VI Preparatory School is proud to offer a dynamic and supportive learning environment that allows each child to thrive academically, emotionally, and socially. The school is situated within 22 acres of beautiful grounds, providing ample space for both indoor and outdoor activities. This exceptional setting, combined with purpose-built classrooms, inspires creativity and offers pupils the opportunity to engage in a range of activities that extend beyond the traditional classroom environment.
The Pre-Prep department at KES Prep provides the foundation for pupils' education, with learning designed to ignite curiosity and foster a love of learning. With small class sizes, every child receives personalised attention to ensure that their individual needs are met. In addition to core subjects, children benefit from specialist teaching in Music, Performing Arts, French, PE, and Forest and Beach School. These enriching experiences allow children to explore their interests and develop a well-rounded skill set. Parental involvement is strongly encouraged through various events such as parent breakfasts, sports days, and assemblies, creating a vibrant and supportive community for all.
As pupils transition to Lower Prep, the learning journey becomes increasingly challenging and dynamic. The curriculum is carefully designed to stretch and inspire pupils, helping them build academic confidence and resilience. Specialist teaching continues in Music, Drama, PE, and Languages, while Outdoor Education and frequent trips — including Year 4’s first residential — allow children to develop independence and explore new areas of interest. Emotional well-being is a strong focus at KES Prep, supporting children to face challenges with resilience and empathy.
One of the distinctive features of KES Prep is its smooth transition to King Edward VI Senior School in Southampton. Pupils who excel in Year 5 are recommended by the Headmistress for progression to the Senior School without the stress of an entrance exam. This approach allows children to focus on their continued growth and development, with the confidence that their hard work and achievements will support their future success.
Families are invited to attend the School in Action Open Morning on Friday 7 February to experience the nurturing environment at KES Prep for themselves. Attendees will have the opportunity to discover how small class sizes, specialist teaching, and outstanding pastoral care support each child’s academic and personal growth.
Booking a place at the Open Morning will provide a first-hand look at how KES Prep can help children reach their full potential.

pageCache.text:
King Edward VI School launches The KES Group, bringing together its schools to shape the future of independent education in Hampshire
King Edward VI School has today announced the launch of The KES Group, bringing together King Edward VI School in Southampton, KES Preparatory School in Romsey, and Prince’s Mead in Winchester as a single, connected family of schools, reinforcing KES as the home of exceptional independent education for children across Hampshire aged 2-18.
This milestone moment formally brings the three schools together to strengthen the experience for pupils and families across the region, creating greater continuity, shared opportunity and access to collective expertise.
At the heart of the Group sits King Edward VI School in Southampton, recently named among the Top 10 schools in the South West in The Sunday Times Parent Power 2026 league tables, based on exceptional A Level and GCSE results in Summer 2025. Its long-standing reputation for academic excellence and values-led education provides the foundation from which the Group grows.
The school was also named a Finalist for Regional Independent School of the Year (South) in the 2025 Independent Schools of the Year Awards, recognition that reflects not only its academic strength, but the clarity of its recently redefined values and Boundless Futures vision, which now unite King Edward VI School, KES Preparatory School and Prince’s Mead in a shared sense of purpose.
The preparatory schools and nurseries in Romsey and Winchester are a vital part of this vision. Both KES Prep and Prince’s Mead bring their own thriving communities and cherished traditions, and their inclusion within The KES Group strengthens the breadth and continuity of independent education offered to families across Hampshire.
Neal Parker, Head of King Edward VI School, said:
“This is a significant moment in the life of our schools. We are proud of the strength of each of our communities and bringing them together more formally allows us to build on that for the benefit of our families across Hampshire.
I am also proud to continue supporting this shared future in a new capacity, as I take on the role of Executive Principal of The KES Group from September 2027, helping to guide the long-term development of our schools.”
The KES Group signals a clear ambition: to continue to be the home of exceptional independent education in Hampshire, bringing together heritage, innovation and a shared commitment to the long-term success of every pupil.
This is a proud moment for the schools, as they look ahead to celebrating 500 years of educating children across Hampshire. Throughout launch week, representatives from across the community, past and present, alongside each Head, will contribute to a time capsule to be placed at Hill Lane, Southampton, and opened in 2053, marking 500 years in the School’s history not only as a moment to honour heritage, but one that helps define its own Boundless Future.

pageCache.text:
The KES Group launch marked by time capsule to be opened at 500th anniversary of King Edward VI School, Southampton in 2053
Earlier this week, King Edward VI School announced the launch of The KES Group, bringing together King Edward VI School in Southampton, KES Preparatory School in Romsey and Prince’s Mead in Winchester, reinforcing KES as the home of exceptional independent education for children across Hampshire aged 2–18.
At the heart of the Group sits King Edward VI School, recently named among the Top 10 schools in the South West in The Sunday Times Parent Power 2026 league tables, based on exceptional A Level and GCSE results. The school was also recognised as a Finalist for Regional Independent School of the Year (South) in the 2025 Independent Schools of the Year Awards, a recognition that reflects not only its academic strength, but the clarity of its recently redefined values and Boundless Futures vision, which now unite King Edward VI School, KES Preparatory School and Prince’s Mead in a shared sense of purpose.
That family extends across Hampshire, with the Preparatory schools and nurseries in Romsey and Winchester playing a vital role. KES Prep and Prince’s Mead bring their own thriving communities and cherished traditions, strengthening the breadth and continuity of education offered to families.
The Head Boy and Head Girl at KES Preparatory School, Logan and Matilda.
Today, that connection is brought to life through the creation of a time capsule, holding a moment in their shared story while looking ahead to the future they are shaping together.
Placed in the grounds at Hill Lane, the capsule will be opened in June 2053, when King Edward VI School celebrates its 500th anniversary. It contains a snapshot of life across the Group in 2026 and the ambitions that will shape the years to come.
The initiative brought together contributions from across the KES community, both past and present. Letters from the Heads of each school sit alongside messages from pupil leaders and pupil voice groups, who wrote directly to future generations, sharing their hopes for the schools and the opportunities they believe lie ahead. Old Edwardians (the school’s alumni) also contributed, ensuring the capsule reflects not only where the schools are today, but the strength of the community that has shaped them over generations.
Neal Parker, Head of King Edward VI School, said:
“As ever, our children are at the heart of every decision we make, so it felt only right to mark this moment in a way that amplifies their voices and reflects their experiences. The time capsule brings together perspectives from across our communities, from age 2 through to 18, capturing what school life means to them today and the hopes they hold for the future.
When it is opened in 2053, it will speak directly to future pupils about the moment our schools came together with a shared purpose.”
The Head Boy and Head Girl at Prince's Mead School, Olly and Anabelle.
As the oldest school in Southampton, King Edward VI School looks ahead to 500 years of educating children across Hampshire, marking a defining moment in its story.
It honours a remarkable heritage while setting the course for its own Boundless Future. The main group photograph: Pupil Leadership Team (Freya, Tom, Elin, Vega), Heads of each School (Neal Parker, Rebecca Smith, Adam King), Chair of Governors (Geraint Davies), and Old Edwardian (Maurice Rowles).

pageCache.text:
KES Prep Supports The Hampshire Hedge Project with Hedgerow Planting
KES Prep proudly played its part in the Hampshire Hedge initiative, an inspiring environmental campaign led by CPRE Hampshire.
Year 5 pupils, staff, and volunteers came together to plant 200 metres of hedgerow on the school grounds, contributing to a vital nature recovery corridor. The Hampshire Hedge project aims to connect the South Downs National Park and the New Forest National Park by creating a continuous network of hedgerows winding through the heart of Hampshire. This ecological corridor links woodlands, meadows, local nature reserves, and Sites of Special Scientific Interest (SSSIs), helping to enhance biodiversity, support wildlife habitats, and tackle climate change.
Mr Caie, Head of Outdoor Learning at KES Prep, said: "We were delighted to be part of the Hampshire Hedge project and to allow our pupils to engage with such an impactful environmental initiative. Planting these hedgerows has not only enriched the habitat potential of our grounds but has also provided an invaluable opportunity to teach our pupils about the importance of conservation. We believe hands-on experience like this will empower them to take an active role in making a positive impact, reinforcing the vital message that small actions can make a big difference in supporting wildlife and preserving the environment."
Since its launch in 2023, the Hampshire Hedge project has made impressive strides, with schools, communities, and volunteers across the county rallying together to make the vision a reality. Once complete, the corridor will stand as a beautiful feature of Hampshire’s landscape, offering critical support to wildlife and the wider ecosystem while connecting key green spaces under increasing development pressure.
KES Prep’s involvement reflected the school’s commitment to environmental education and sustainability. The planting day was an engaging and rewarding experience, inspiring pupils to take pride in caring for the natural world.
Together with CPRE Hampshire, KES Prep is proud to contribute to this ground-breaking campaign, helping to create greener spaces for future generations to enjoy. KES Prep has been recognised as for its outdoor learning provision, and has been praised for outstanding achievement in sustainable development education and management and continually improves the environmental performance of the School and the wider community.

pageCache.pageTitle: King Edward VI Preparatory School Opens New Natural Playscape for Pre Prep - Latest News | Community | KES Prep
pageCache.text:
King Edward VI Preparatory School Opens New Natural Playscape for Pre Prep
King Edward VI Preparatory School in Romsey has recently opened a new natural playscape for pupils in Reception and Year 1, designed to encourage imagination, exploration and unstructured play.
At KES Prep, outdoor learning and play are a central part of the educational ethos, particularly in the early years and Pre-Prep. For Reception and Year 1 pupils, play is not simply a break from learning - it is learning. Through play, children develop confidence, resilience, communication skills and creativity. Climbing, balancing, building and exploring together helps pupils learn to take risks, solve problems and interact with others in meaningful ways.
Created in partnership with specialist play designers Earth Wrights, the space reflects a shared belief that children thrive when given the freedom to explore, experiment and invent their own games.
Since opening, the response from pupils, staff and families has been overwhelmingly positive. Staff have already noticed a real shift in how children are playing together with more collaboration, creativity and confidence as they explore the space and create their own adventures.
Jo Humphreys, Head of Pre Prep said: "It was a privilege to work with Earth Wrights to create a playscape that truly places children at its heart. Our vision was to design a space filled with limitless possibilities, somewhere where learning, imagination and adventure naturally unfold. By incorporating a wide range of moveable, open‑ended structures and resources, the environment can transform from one day to the next, shaped entirely by the children’s ideas and interactions. Watching them explore, collaborate and make the space their own is joyful and reflects the very best of childhood"
The project also reflects the school’s commitment to sustainability. Earth Wrights are pioneers in natural play design, using durable materials sourced responsibly and avoiding plastics wherever possible. Much of the equipment is built from FSC-certified Robinia wood, chosen for its natural strength and longevity, allowing structures to be created without chemical treatments.
By working with the natural landscape and using sustainable materials, the playscape not only provides a rich environment for play but also helps children develop an early appreciation for the natural world.

pageCache.text:
ISI Inspection Report
We are delighted to share our Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) school inspection report with you. This is the culmination of five years of hard work from the staff team, building on the success of the last report in November 2019. ISI inspections now look to determine whether schools meet the standards in five key areas.
The inspection team found that we meet all of the standards in all five key areas, and below are highlights from each of the five sections of the report:
Leadership and Management, and Governance
The inspection team recognised that the senior team have high expectations that permeate all aspects of school life, and that the wellbeing and happiness of pupils is central to the work of a cohesive staff team.
Quality of Education, Training and Recreation
The inspection team acknowledged that the pupils make at least expected progress, and in many cases better than expected progress, including those pupils with SEND. This is due to careful planning of lessons and skillful delivery by knowledgeable staff.
Pupil’s Physical and Mental Health and Emotional Wellbeing
The inspection team noted that our children display high levels of self-control and respect in their behaviour towards others due to high expectations and a consultative and empathetic approach to behaviour management; with staff acting as influential role models in demonstrating courtesy and warmth.
Pupil’s Social and Economic Education and Contribution to Society
The inspection team identified that our embedded culture and values enable children to understand right from wrong and take pride in their diverse and inclusive community; and that this in turn bolsters their social confidence and creates resilient learners, undaunted by failure and keen to do better.
Safeguarding
The inspection team found that the safeguarding arrangements were appropriate and robustly implemented, and that children feel safe and secure at the school.
Recommended Next Steps
All schools receive at least one area for development. At KES Prep we are always looking at ways to make our curriculum as real world ready as possible, and to encourage our children to think critically and problem solve.. Our recommended next step – to increase opportunities for older pupils to develop their skills in independent critical enquiry – is something we can’t wait to develop. We know that this approach, already embedded in our Early Years and Pre-Prep, facilitates creativity, critical thinking and deep understanding – all whilst making learning collaborative and engaging.
